title: Cloud-Aware EO–SAR Collection: Recovering Optical Passes with Radar Under Partial Cloud Cover
content: Optical (EO) collection from low Earth orbit fails when cloud opacity exceeds the sensor threshold, so an EO-only policy wastes access windows under partial cloud. We study a small mixed constellation (3 EO + 2 SAR) tasking three fixed areas of interest (AOIs) under a spatiotemporal cloud field. EO succeeds only when site opacity is below 0.35; SAR succeeds in weather at lower quality weight (0.55). On a MIXED preset, EO-only greedy achieves 3.6 successful collects per episode and 33.3% confirmed AOI coverage, while a phenomenology heuristic that collects with EO when predicted clear and with SAR when cloudy reaches 33.8 collects/episode and 100% coverage—about +30 collects/episode and +67 percentage points in coverage. An ablation shows that removing the discrete tip channel changes throughput by only ∼0.2 collects/episode; the operational content is dual-sensor tasking, not the tip bits. Shared-policy proximal policy optimization (PPO) with local observations and invalid-action masking learns from untrained performance (∼3 collects/episode) to about 42 collects/episode on MIXED, matching or exceeding the heuristic. Under partial cloud, EO-only tasking loses most successful collects; a dual-sensor policy that uses SAR when EO is blocked recovers on the order of +30 collects/episode and full AOI coverage in this simulation. The discrete tip channel is secondary; shared PPO can learn the dual-sensor rule. Results are from a controlled simulation, not flight data.
